course_name_original: Additive Fertigung und Materialien für Werkzeuge

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have comprehensive knowledge of various additive manufacturing processes for both plastic and metal components. They will know the specific requirements for raw materials and the production of plastic filaments and metal powders for 3D printing. Furthermore, they will be familiar with the basic requirements for metallic tooling materials and with different types of tool steels.

Students will have a detailed understanding of how to evaluate 3D printed components and can compare them with products from conventional processes. They will gain in-depth knowledge of heat treatment of steels for plastics processing and will be familiar with methods of thermal analysis as well as thermochemical surface treatments, including case hardening and nitriding, and with coating concepts for such products.

Students will be able to use the acquired knowledge to understand the role of diffusion in thermochemical surface treatments. They can apply design guidelines for additive manufacturing processes and demonstrate the possibilities of these technologies. Their knowledge will enable them to assess the applicability and efficiency of tooling materials for specific production purposes.
Students will be able to practically apply their acquired knowledge to produce prototypes using 3D printing processes.

Students will prepare the results obtained from practical experiments in a team. Subsequently, the results will be discussed, taking into account the learned material and supplementary technical literature, and communicated in an appropriate form.

syllabus_topics:
Processes of additive manufacturing for plastic components (FDM/FFF, SLA, DLP, MJF, SLS, 
)

Processes of additive manufacturing for metallic components (L-PBF, Binder Jetting, 
)
Evaluation of 3D printed components and comparison with products from conventional processes
Possibilities, design guidelines and application examples
Production of plastic filaments and metal powders for 3D printing
Heat treatment of steels for plastics processing using methods of thermal analysis
Thermochemical surface engineering (case hardening and nitriding) and coating concepts
Role of diffusion in thermochemical surface treatments
assessment_rules: The choice of examination type (written or oral) is at the discretion of the examiners and will be communicated to students at the beginning of the semester. The duration and scope for the written exam are according to the valid study regulations, and for the oral exam according to the General Part of the Examination Regulations (ATPO). The unassessed experimental work corresponds to the scope of laboratory activities (approx. 4 - 6 experiments).
